data.one_liner: Flutter runtime permissions made easy with adaptive dialogs and permission gates.
data.what_it_does: Simplifies handling runtime permissions in Flutter by wrapping permission_handler with one-line requests, adaptive dialogs, rationale flows, and settings round-trips. It also provides a PermissionGate widget to wrap UI that requires specific permissions.
use_when: You need to request permissions with automatic adaptive explanation and settings dialogs.
You want to guard UI widgets behind a permission check using PermissionGate.
You need a robust fallback flow when permissions are permanently denied or restricted.
avoid_when: You need permission handling on macOS or Linux platforms, which are not supported.
You prefer writing custom platform permission dialogs and state management from scratch.
strengths: Handles complex permission flows (denied, permanently denied, restricted) automatically.
Includes a PermissionGate widget that re-checks status when returning to the foreground.
Provides built-in testing support with FakeSmartPermissionGateway.
weaknesses: Relies on permission_handler and inherits its platform limitations (no macOS or Linux support).
Requires platform-specific configuration in AndroidManifest.xml, Info.plist, and optionally Podfile.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding permissions to AndroidManifest.xml, usage descriptions to iOS Info.plist, configuring Gradle compileSdk, and optionally setting up Podfile macros for iOS CocoaPods.

alternatives.name: permission_handler
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer direct, low-level control over permission requests and status checking without the added UI flows, dialogs, and widgets provided by smart_permission.
